en.name: Curry leaves
en.summary: Fresh curry leaves keep 7–10 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 1–2 months in the freezer. Both figures are borrowed from the general entry for fresh herbs — no agency publishes one for curry leaves — and freezing beats drying for this particular leaf.
en.pantry: No room-temperature timeline is published for curry leaves. They are a fresh, glossy leaf on a woody sprig, and in a warm kitchen they go limp within a day or two and lose their aroma as they do. The extension method for fresh herbs works if you want them out on the counter for a short time: trim the stems, stand them in an inch of water like a bouquet, cover loosely with a bag so air can still circulate, and change the water daily — herbs may last up to a week that way. Otherwise they belong in the fridge.
en.fridge: 7–10 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and this figure is read across from fresh herbs generally rather than measured for curry leaves. Leave them on the stem, do not wash them until you cook, and keep them in a closed box lined with dry kitchen paper — wet leaves blacken within two days. If you do wash them, do it in cool running water without soap or bleach, and dry them thoroughly. Curry leaves lose their aroma fast once they go limp, and a blackened leaf has nothing left to give.
en.freezer: 1–2 months, also read across from fresh herbs. Freezing beats drying for this leaf: freeze whole sprigs dry in a bag and drop them straight into hot oil from frozen. They will not be crisp, but the aroma survives, which it does not in the dried leaf sold in jars — dried curry leaves are a much weaker product and are barely the same ingredient.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Take the sprigs out and drop them straight into hot oil or a tempering pan; thawed leaves go limp and wet.
spoilage: Blackened leaves, usually from moisture in the container.
Leaves that have gone limp and dull with no scent when crushed.
Slime on the stems or leaves.
Mould in a box that was closed on damp leaves.
tips: Leave them on the stem until you cook; stripped leaves dry out fast.
Line the box with dry kitchen paper and do not wash until use.
Freeze whole sprigs and use them straight from frozen.
Buy a big bunch when you see one and freeze most of it; they are hard to find fresh.

faq.q: How long do fresh curry leaves keep?
faq.a: 7–10 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 1–2 months frozen. Both figures are read across from fresh herbs in general.
Yes, and it is the best way to keep them. Freeze whole sprigs dry in a bag and drop them into hot oil from frozen; the aroma survives.

faq.q: Are dried curry leaves the same thing?
faq.a: Not really. Drying takes most of the aroma with it, so the jarred leaves are a much weaker ingredient than frozen fresh ones.

zh.name: 咖哩葉
zh.summary: 新鮮咖哩葉放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 7～10 天，冷凍 1～2 個月。這兩個數字都是從「新鮮香草」的通用資料借過來的——沒有機關為咖哩葉公布期限——而對這種葉子來說，冷凍的效果勝過乾燥。
zh.pantry: 咖哩葉沒有公布的室溫期限。它是長在木質細枝上、油亮的新鮮葉片，在溫暖的廚房裡一兩天就會軟掉，香氣也跟著走。如果只是想短時間放在檯面上，推廣單位對新鮮香草的做法可以用：把莖剪一下、插進約兩三公分深的水裡像一束花，上面鬆鬆罩個袋子讓空氣還能流通，每天換水——這樣香草大約可以撐一週。否則，它該待的地方是冰箱。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 7～10 天；這個數字是比照一般新鮮香草而來，不是針對咖哩葉測出來的。請讓葉子留在枝上，要下鍋時才洗，並且裝在鋪了乾廚房紙巾的密閉盒裡——濕掉的葉子兩天內就會發黑。真的要洗，就用冷的流水沖，不要用清潔劑或漂白水，洗完徹底擦乾。咖哩葉一旦軟掉，香氣散得很快，而發黑的葉子已經什麼都給不了了。
zh.freezer: 1～2 個月，同樣是比照新鮮香草而來。對這種葉子來說，冷凍勝過乾燥：把整枝擦乾、裝袋冷凍，要用時直接從冷凍丟進熱油裡。它不會是脆的，但香氣留得住——而那正是罐裝乾咖哩葉留不住的東西，乾燥咖哩葉弱得多，幾乎稱不上是同一種材料。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。直接把枝條從冷凍拿出來丟進熱油或爆香鍋裡；解凍過的葉子會軟塌出水。
spoilage: 葉子發黑，通常是容器裡有水氣造成的。
葉子軟塌暗沉，搓一下也沒有香氣。
葉子還濕就密封的盒子裡長霉。
tips: 下鍋前都讓葉子留在枝上；摘下來的葉子乾得很快。
盒子鋪乾廚房紙巾，要用時才洗。
整枝冷凍，直接從冷凍取用。
看到大把的就買下來、大部分冷凍；新鮮咖哩葉並不好找。

faq.q: 新鮮咖哩葉可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 7～10 天，或冷凍 1～2 個月。兩個數字都是比照一般新鮮香草而來。
可以，而且這是保存它最好的方式。整枝擦乾裝袋冷凍，要用時直接丟進熱油，香氣留得住。

faq.q: 乾燥咖哩葉是同一種東西嗎？
faq.a: 算不上。乾燥會把大部分香氣帶走，所以罐裝乾葉比冷凍的新鮮葉弱很多。
